title: Page Image Height (Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the pixel height to use when rendering a document page as an image. Controls the vertical resolution of the rasterized output.

## When to use
Set this parameter alongside [Page Image Width](https://capdag.com/browse/media:page-image-width;textable;numeric) when you need to control the full resolution of rendered pages. Increasing height improves vertical detail for tall or portrait-oriented documents.

## Notes
Valid range: 50–4000 pixels. Aspect ratio handling is machine-specific. For most document types, setting only width and allowing the machine to infer height is simpler and avoids distortion.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
